Lane `check/M0-a-05-close-s3` ran on Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, on the owner's Windows 11 PC (WSL2 Ubuntu, Linux x64,
Node 24.12.0, machine id `wsl:Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz:20cpu:16gib`), in flow flow-7, stage group S.

This seat is an implementer-side independent checker. It is not the item's author; the author lanes are `build/M0-a-05`,

`-s1.md` and `-s2.md` were left unchanged.

This seat ran no git command and changed no file of the item. Vitest worker counts came from `tools/test_budget.py`
(J197): 6 and 4 for the gates in the tree, 1 for each B-FUZZ seed and each mutant. `free -m` showed 7.5 GB to 12.3 GB

They were deleted afterwards, `node_modules` first. The logs are kept in those scratch folders.

The insert sources were the same bytes for the whole check. `sha256sum` of `packages/kernel/src/insert/*.ts` at 19:56

## Verdict: FAIL

Fix round S3 closes N-42's two named repros. The ninth chain now commits in all eight variants, and the B-FUZZ seed
−1863295922 is green. It does not close N-42's class, and it does not address N-43 at all. Every S3 source file was
last written by 17:29, after N-43 was ruled at 16:55, but no S3 file, test or choices row mentions N-43. Six lines
fail:

1. **N-42's class remains open.** Two mandatory chains are still refused `E_INVARIANT` "no route … keeps clearance"
   on the final code. These are M0-a-08 fix1's buffer cases.
2. **B-FUZZ, the item's here-bar, is red on a fresh seed.** At `PLAT_FUZZ_SEED=31337`, the random family THROWS at
   case 3 624. The same throw happens on S2's code.
3. **N-43 A still throws.** Its regression is not pinned.
4. **N-43 B, the fidelity bound, is not implemented.** The routes are still 2 711 cm and 2 175 cm off their segments,
   and no test asserts the bound.
5. **The brief's s3-inflight case (a) still throws.**
6. **Seven targeted mutants survive.** Each one breaks a bound that C-0209 states for the new fallback routes.

## 3. Mutants (this seat's own, planned before reading the author's self-check notes)

Sixteen targeted mutants were run, each aimed at a promise C-0209 or C-0210 states. Each ran in its own mirror on the
item folder at `PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=1000` with `--maxWorkers=1`. BASE was 136/136. Each mutant was also run through the
seven repros of part 1 (the einvariant repro, fix1 cases 1 and 2, the s160 throw, s60 and s25), and its output was
diffed against BASE.

| id | mutation | step3-5 at 10³ | repros | judgement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KB | the far-end re-landing reports no `W_PLACED` | `3 failed \| 133 passed` | — | killed |
| KH | `alongEdge` accepts an edge running the opposite way (`dot !== 0`) | `56 failed \| 80 passed` | — | killed |
| KS | the sliver route is accepted without its clearance check | `3 failed \| 133 passed` | fix1 cases 1 and 2 THROW instead of refusing | killed |
| **KA** | the re-landing bound is `8 · attractCm²` (2 · √2 · `attractCm`) instead of √2 · `attractCm` | 136/136 | same | **survives; non-equivalent** — C-0209: "a re-landed vertex moves at most √2 · `attractCm`". Where every candidate within the bound fails, the mutant lands up to 73.5 cm off. Nothing pins the bound. |
| **KC** | `freeSince` ignores whether the vertex has edges | 136/136 | same | **survives; non-equivalent** — C-0209: "whose end is a free vertex this op just placed (`freeSince`: new, no edge)". A point landed by a split is new in the journal but has edges, so the mutant would roll back the split and move an attracted vertex. |
| **KE** | the sliver route replaces any vertex landing, not only the endpoint fallback | 136/136 | same | **survives; non-equivalent** — C-0209: "where a crossing's landing is the placement's endpoint fallback". The mutant overrides a landing within `attractCm`. |
| **KF** | the sliver partner counts within 2 · `minEdge` | 136/136 | same | **survives; non-equivalent** — C-0209 defines the partner as "closer than `minEdge`". The mutant places crossings across gaps that are not slivers. |
| **KG** | `placeAcross` searches within 2 · `attractCm` | 136/136 | same | **survives; non-equivalent** — C-0209: "the across placement within `attractCm` of the exact crossing". |
| **KN** | `E_WORK_LIMIT` during a far-end candidate's route no longer ends the op | 136/136 | same | **survives; non-equivalent** — C-0209: "E_WORK_LIMIT ends the op". Without a free near end, the mutant returns `E_INVARIANT` instead. |
| **KP** | re-landing candidates of any level (`> n` filter removed) | 136/136 | same | **survives; non-equivalent** — C-0209: "the nearest existing vertex of level ≤ n". The mutant lands a chain on a finer vertex, which §3.3 treats as kept content. |
| KD | the sliver route judged by `clearSince` instead of `clearWholeSince` | 136/136 | same | survives; the author's equivalence argument (`placeAcross`'s (iii) already checks the split sub-edges' rows) was not refuted. Note N-11 |
| KI | `alongEdge` without the `dot < l2` bound | 136/136 | same | equivalent: on a valid arena, an edge from a running collinear to or past b would be the edge a–b (shared earlier) or would put b inside an edge |
| KL | the re-landing candidate filter (closer than `minEdge` to the other end with no piece joining them) removed | 136/136 | same | PLAUSIBLY equivalent: two such unjoined vertices would already break §3.10, and attraction lands within `attractCm`. Note N-11 |
| KO | the re-landing is allowed when the point was landed earlier in the op | 136/136 | same | PLAUSIBLY equivalent in effect (the moved vertex is still a free one the op placed). Note N-11 |
| KQ | at most 1 re-landing candidate instead of 8 | 136/136 | same | survives; it is consistent with C-0209's words ("at most 8"), but no case pins a second candidate. Note N-11 |
| KR | `routeSegment` no longer returns the endpoint route's non-`E_INVARIANT` refusal | 136/136 | same | survives; this is S1's line (N-4's class, the strict route's refusal). Note N-11 |

The survival of each mutant is CONFIRMED, by the run and the identical repro output. The judgement of each as
non-equivalent is CONFIRMED by reading the code against C-0209's stated bounds. Whether any honest input reaches the
difference is PLAUSIBLE, not measured: the fallback routes are reached only on rare inputs (C-0209 counts 1 in 70 000),
and every pin of them is a single repro case. Under the brief, a survivor on a stated promise that this seat does not
find equivalent is a blocker. KA, KC, KE, KF, KG, KN and KP are that.

## 6. What the next round needs (from the failing lines; the round's design is the author's)

* Make every clearance failure on a mandatory chain a `KernelResult`, never a throw. This covers `insertChain.ts:649`'s
  `checkClearance`, which N-6 already noted. Pin s160 (N-43 A) and seed 31337 path 3623 as named regressions.
* Close N-42's class for fix1 case 1 (no free end: all five routes break clearance) and case 2 (re-landing finds no
  candidate). Pin both.
* Implement N-43 B's bound on the design route's endpoint fallback (`placePoint` → `endpoint` far along the edge). Pin
  s60 and s25. Assert the Hausdorff bound on every mandatory commit in B-FUZZ and in a property of its own. Otherwise,
  return BLOCKED with a minimal repro, as N-43 orders.
* Pin the bounds KA, KC, KE, KF, KG, KN and KP mutate, with constructed cases that reach the fallback routes.
